name: Supabase
summary: Supabase is a hosted Postgres database that comes with a ready-made API, realtime updates, and login built in.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan: 500 MB database, 5 GB egress, 50,000 monthly active users, but the project pauses after 7 days with no activity.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Pro plan starts at $25/month per project: 8 GB disk, 100 GB storage, 250 GB egress, 100,000 MAU, then usage-based overage.

portability.note: It is standard Postgres, so you can dump and restore the database to any other Postgres host with little rework.

storage_model.note: Supabase runs and manages the Postgres server for you in the cloud.

data_model.note: Supabase's database is Postgres, a standard SQL relational database.

realtime_built_in.note: Supabase Realtime streams database inserts, updates, and deletes to connected browsers over websockets, no extra service needed.

serverless_friendly.note: A built-in pooler (Supavisor) and an HTTP API (PostgREST) both work well from serverless functions.

mobile_sdk.note: Official SDKs exist for Flutter, Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android), and React Native through the JS client.

setup.step: Create a free Supabase account and a new project at supabase.com.
Scaffold a Next.js app with the official Supabase starter template, which installs @supabase/supabase-js and @supabase/ssr for you.
Copy the Project URL and publishable key from the project's Connect panel in the dashboard.
Add the URL and key to your environment file.
Create a table in the SQL editor and turn on Row Level Security with a policy before reading or writing from the app.

builder_notes: Use the publishable key in browser code and keep the secret key only on the server; never expose the secret key to the browser.
Turn on Row Level Security on every table and add a policy; without one, the API leaves the table unprotected.
In serverless or edge functions use the pooled connection string, not the direct one, since the free tier caps direct connections at 60.
